clue.text: Boy's entertaining run down wood

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: 'Boy!' as an exclamation of surprise is the same as 'Wow!'; the 's is 'is'
feeling run down means feeling unwell, ill

explanation.surface: A lad is busy amusing someone who is feeling under the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boy' looks like a lad, but it is the exclamation, as in 'Boy, that was close!'
explanation.definitionFit: Willow is a tree and its timber, used for cricket bats.

clue.text: Female group on settee regularly boosted dry fower

parts.note: WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word
boosted means lifted up, which in a down answer reads the word bottom to top

parts.note: to air washing is to dry it

explanation.surface: Women's club members on a sofa keep getting raised up, as a parched flower would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' belongs to the wordplay, so the definition is only 'fower', the printed spelling of flower; 'regularly' takes alternate letters of settee and 'boosted' reads AIR upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisteria is a climbing plant with drooping lilac blossoms.

clue.text: Conservationists in pastureland close by, listened

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or pasture
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage conservation body
near means close by

explanation.surface: Conservation volunteers in a nearby field paid attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend an ear is an idiom meaning to listen attentively.

clue.text: Russian skimmed river there?

indicators.note: skimmed means the top is taken off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: the Volga is Russia's longest river

explanation.surface: A Russian skimmed over the water there?
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the top is the first letter, so 'skimmed' takes V off the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Olga is a common Russian girl's name, so it stands for a Russian person.

clue.text: Runner satisfed injured leg getting right

parts.note: smug means self-satisfied

indicators.note: an injured leg is a damaged one, so its letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: An athlete pleased with himself hurts a leg but gets things right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' makes GLE from LEG. 'Runner' suggests an athlete; here it is a contraband runner. 'satisfed' is the printed spelling of satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs goods illegally across a border is a smuggler: rum-runner, gun-runner.

clue.text: Publication number 12's about lecturer and explorer

parts.note: mag is short for magazine

indicators.note: about means around, so the other answer surrounds the letter

parts.note: the answer to 12 across, a word meaning style

explanation.surface: A magazine article on lecturers and an adventurer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside ELAN, the answer to 12 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferdinand Magellan led the first expedition to sail round the world.

clue.text: Amount of work raised by wardens ordering turf

indicators.note: raised means lifted, which in a down answer reads the word upwards

parts.note: an erg is a unit of work in physics

indicators.note: ordering means arranging, so the letters of wardens are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Park wardens give orders about a lawn, raising the workload.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns ERG into GRE; 'ordering' makes ENSWARD from WARDENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Greensward is a poetic term for grassy ground, a stretch of lawn.

clue.text: Pause, as the Parisian put on something woolly

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece put on another sits above it

parts.note: le is French for the
a tup is a ram, a woolly animal

explanation.surface: Like a Parisian, wear a woolly jumper while taking a break.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-up is a slackening or lull in activity.

clue.text: Some of county documents seized by criminal gang

indicators.note: seized by means held inside the gang

parts.note: a ring is a gang of criminals
ID is short for identity documents

explanation.surface: Papers from part of the county are taken by gangsters.
explanation.walkthrough: A riding was one of the three divisions of Yorkshire, a large county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire was divided into three ridings, administrative districts of the county.

clue.text: Flower beginning to limp in thunder

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the noise

parts.note: boom is the deep roar of thunder

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A flower starts to droop during a thunderstorm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside BOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloom is a blossom on a plant.

clue.text: US elite soldier gathers information about republic

indicators.note: to gather is to take in, so the soldier holds the other piece

parts.note: a SEAL is a member of the US Navy's special forces

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the slang word is read backwards

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: An American special-forces man collects intelligence on a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US elite soldier' looks like the definition; the country is the republic at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a West African country with a republican constitution.

clue.text: Current newsman touring Spain was invited on show

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so the current wraps the country's letter

parts.note: a gust is a sudden current of air
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
ED, short for editor, is a common crossword newsman

explanation.surface: A topical journalist travelling round Spain was asked onto a programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day' describing the newsman; it is a gust of wind. 'touring' puts E inside GUST.
explanation.definitionFit: To guest is to appear as a visiting performer on someone else's programme.

clue.text: Style of journalese that's revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the run of letters is read right to left
of signals that the letters come from within the next word

explanation.surface: A remark on a radical brand of newspaper writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'journalese' sits NALE, which 'that's revolutionary' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is flair or dash, a stylish verve in how something is done.

clue.text: Possibly nip to get kitchen implement

parts.note: the word pin, rolled over so its letters run backwards, gives the word nip

explanation.surface: Perhaps nip out to buy something for the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer read as instructions, 'roll PIN', produces NIP, which is what the clue shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden cylinder for flattening pastry is a standard piece of baking equipment.

clue.text: Tory politician welcomes partner back working shift

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the politician holds the other piece

parts.note: Michael Gove is a Conservative politician

indicators.note: back means reversed, so the partner word is read backwards

parts.note: a mate is a partner
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: A Conservative MP greets a spouse returning from a work shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a work shift; here it is the verb meaning hurry up.
explanation.definitionFit: Get a move on is an idiom urging someone to hurry, to get going.

clue.text: Ancient tribe briefy consume writer making archaeological discoveries?

indicators.note: to consume is to take in, so one piece swallows the other
briefly means cut short, so the tribe's name loses its final letter

parts.note: the Iceni were the British tribe led by Boudicca
the writer of a clue is referred to as me

explanation.surface: A short-lived old tribe feeds on an author who is digging up the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefy' is the printed spelling of briefly. The question mark flags a definition by example: frozen bodies such as Otzi.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient bodies preserved in glaciers, like the Alpine find Otzi, are prized archaeological finds.

clue.text: Castle rejected bare piece of candle

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: raw means exposed, bare
the wick is the string part of a candle

explanation.surface: A fortress turns away a naked bit of a candle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns RAW into WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Warwick Castle is a famous medieval fortress in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Accountant to attach guide, in a respectful way

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
to pin is to attach
to hand someone is to guide them with the hand, as into a carriage

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper fixes up a guide, behaving deferentially.
explanation.definitionFit: Cap in hand describes approaching humbly and deferentially, as if holding one's hat.

clue.text: Rotund Oxbridge sportsperson coming over books transport

indicators.note: coming over means covering, so the sportsperson wraps the books

parts.note: a Blue is someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge in sport
B is book, so BB is books
RY is railway, a means of transport

explanation.surface: A tubby university athlete brings books over on transport.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is awarded to those who compete for Oxford or Cambridge University against the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Blubbery means fat and flabby, like whale blubber.

clue.text: Sycophant easy to unravel in time

indicators.note: in places the jumble inside the period of time

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: to unravel means to come apart, so the letters of easy are disordered

explanation.surface: A flatterer finds things easy to sort out in time.
explanation.walkthrough: A yea-sayer always says yes; the period of time is split after its third letter to take in the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes-man who agrees with everything is a sycophant.

clue.text: Sentimental attempt to take up lace embroidering

indicators.note: to take up is to absorb, so the attempt holds the other piece

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: embroidering means working decoratively, so the letters of lace are worked into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A soppy effort to start doing needlework on lace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embroidering' makes EACL from LACE; the lace looks like the thing being stitched.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacly means cloyingly sweet, like syrup, hence mawkishly sentimental.

clue.text: Recording level loud, refecting booze

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical direction for loud

indicators.note: reflecting (as printed, refecting) means mirrored, so the two words are read backwards together

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
par means level, equal

explanation.surface: Turning up the volume on a recording while thinking about drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refecting' (printed thus, for reflecting) turns the two words together into RAPPE; 'level' looks like an audio level but means par.
explanation.definitionFit: A frappe is an iced drink, often liqueur poured over crushed ice.

clue.text: Actor's last performance perhaps given a cry of approval

definitions.meaning: a shout of joy or praise, hooray

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense leans on the phrase 'last hurrah', a final appearance before retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a final show, from the idiom, and a cheer of delight.

clue.text: Britain's peak 90 degrees — it's savage

indicators.note: a peak is the top, which in a down answer is the first letter

parts.note: east is the compass bearing of 90 degrees

explanation.surface: Britain's mountain at a right angle is a wild one.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute, someone cruel and uncivilised, is a beast.

clue.text: Peaceful 'ound with foreign bread heading for doghouse

parts.note: to hound is to hunt; with the h dropped as the apostrophe shows, hound becomes 'unt
bread is slang for money, and the rouble is Russia's

indicators.note: heading means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A dog with some foreign loaf is making for its kennel in a calm state.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''ound' tells the solver to drop the H from the synonym too, so HUNT becomes UNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Untroubled means free from worry, calm and at ease.

clue.text: Unstable coastal tract upset journey's end

indicators.note: upset means turned over, which in a down answer reads the word upwards

parts.note: a spit is a narrow point of land running into the sea

indicators.note: end picks the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: An unsteady stretch of coast is turned over at the journey's close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SPIT into TIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipsy means slightly drunk and so unsteady on one's feet.

clue.text: Load old paper back-to-front

indicators.note: back-to-front means reversed, so the paper's name is read backwards

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: Weight of an out-of-date newspaper read the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-to-front' turns SUN into NUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or duty one must bear.

clue.text: Grappling maths problem with Oscar

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Wrestling with a maths problem alongside Oscar.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the Japanese style of wrestling, a grappling sport.

clue.text: Stuffed agent authorised end of barbecue

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent
to let is to allow, authorise

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A salesman permitted to finish off the barbecue is full.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means full up after eating, gorged.

clue.text: High-pitched broadcaster defends that French article

indicators.note: to defend is to protect by surrounding, so the broadcaster wraps the rest

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster
que is French for that
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A shrill television company stands up for a French piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that French article' looks like one phrase, le or la; it is que (that, in French) plus the English A.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeaky voice or noise is thin and shrill, at a high pitch.

clue.text: Over there — amongst fruit — the ancient festival site

indicators.note: amongst signals one piece placed within another

parts.note: a haw is the red berry of the hawthorn
yon is an old word for over there
ye is an archaic spelling of the

explanation.surface: A distant place among fruit trees is where the old festival is held.
explanation.walkthrough: HAY-ON-WYE is a Welsh border town famous for its literary festival.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh book town hosts a celebrated annual literature festival.

clue.text: Bird misdirected staff on party

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it

parts.note: Con is the standard abbreviation for the Conservative party

indicators.note: misdirected means sent the wrong way, so the letters of the stick are rearranged

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A bird sends a stick in the wrong direction at a gathering.
